## 本节考纲要求

本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 2.5：把 reverse differentiation 扩展到 $e^{ax+b}$、$1/(ax+b)$、$\sin(ax+b)$、$\cos(ax+b)$ 和 $\sec^2(ax+b)$；使用 trigonometric relationships 进行 integration；理解并使用 trapezium rule 估计 definite integral，并判断 over-estimate 或 under-estimate。

工作区没有独立的 Paper 2 note PDF，因此 worked examples 使用同一套 Integration note PDF 中已经独立提取的相关原始图片；每个例题单独成卡。真题全部来自本地 Paper 2 原始 PDF，题干只把 PDF 排版规范为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目。
:::

## 1. Core knowledge

::: {.formula-panel}
### Reverse differentiation

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int e^{ax+b}\,dx&=\frac1a e^{ax+b}+C,\\
\int\frac{1}{ax+b}\,dx&=\frac1a\ln|ax+b|+C,\\
\int\sin(ax+b)\,dx&=-\frac1a\cos(ax+b)+C,\\
\int\cos(ax+b)\,dx&=\frac1a\sin(ax+b)+C,\\
\int\sec^2(ax+b)\,dx&=\frac1a\tan(ax+b)+C.
\end{aligned}
$$

Paper 2 不要求 general substitution method；这里的重点是认出 reverse chain rule，并把 coefficient $a$ 除掉。
:::

::: {.worked-example}
<span class="we-tag">Worked example · Integration note p.13</span>

::: {.formula-panel}
### Trigonometric relationships before integrating

常用恒等式包括

$$
\sin^2x=\frac{1-\cos2x}{2},
\qquad
\cos^2x=\frac{1+\cos2x}{2},
$$

以及

$$
\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x,
\qquad
\sin x\cot\frac{x}{2}=1+\cos x.
$$

先把 integrand 化成 standard integral，再积分；不要在还没有化简时直接套公式。
:::

<span class="we-tag">Worked example · Integration note p.19</span>

![Substitution example](../assets/notes/integration/worked-example-03.webp){.note-figure fig-alt="Original extracted integration note worked example with a composite trigonometric integral"}
:::

::: {.formula-panel}
### Definite integration

若 $F'(x)=f(x)$，则

$$
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a).
$$

每一步都保留上下限；若出现 logarithm，要使用

$$
\ln u-\ln v=\ln\left(\frac uv\right).
$$
:::

::: {.worked-example}
<span class="we-tag">Worked example · Integration note p.22</span>

![Substitution and initial condition](../assets/notes/integration/worked-example-04.webp){.note-figure fig-alt="Original extracted integration note worked example using a definite integral and an initial condition"}
:::

::: {.formula-panel}
### Trapezium rule

把区间 $[a,b]$ 分成 $n$ 个等宽小区间，$h=(b-a)/n$，则

$$
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx
\approx\frac h2\left[y_0+y_n+2(y_1+y_2+\cdots+y_{n-1})\right].
$$

若 $f$ 在区间内 concave down，chords 位于 curve 下方，trapezium rule 给出 under-estimate；若 concave up，则给出 over-estimate。
:::

::: {.formula-panel}
### Further standard integrals

Note 中还包括

$$
\int\tan x\,dx=\ln|\sec x|+C,qquad
\int\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx=\ln|f(x)|+C.
$$

遇到 $\tan(ax+b)$ 或 $f'(ax+b)/(f(ax+b))$ 时，先识别 reverse chain rule 并除以 inner coefficient。若出现 $\sin^2x$ 或 $\cos^2x$，先用 double-angle identities 化成可直接积分的形式。
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Definite integrals and numerical estimates

定积分代入上下限时先计算完整 antiderivative，再做 upper minus lower；不要把 indefinite constant $C$ 带入最终结果。若题目要求 trapezium rule，$[a,b]$ 分成 $n$ 等份、$h=(b-a)/n$，则

$$
\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\approx\frac h2\left[y_0+y_n+2\sum_{r=1}^{n-1}y_r\right].
$$

Concave down 时 trapezium rule 通常是 under-estimate，concave up 时通常是 over-estimate；若题目问 area，要根据图像决定 signed integral 是否需要拆分。
:::

::: {.question-card #p2-int-q01}
### Question 1 · 9709/21/M/J/20 Q7(a–b)

(a) Find the quotient when

$$
9x^3-6x^2-20x+1
$$

is divided by $(3x+2)$, and show that the remainder is $9$.

(b) Hence find

$$
\int_1^6\frac{9x^3-6x^2-20x+1}{3x+2}\,dx,
$$

giving the answer in the form $a+\ln b$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. **[3+5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) Polynomial division gives

$$
9x^3-6x^2-20x+1=(3x+2)(3x^2-4x-4)+9.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{\text{quotient}=3x^2-4x-4,\qquad \text{remainder}=9}.
$$

(b) Use the division result:

$$
\frac{9x^3-6x^2-20x+1}{3x+2}=3x^2-4x-4+\frac9{3x+2}.
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_1^6\frac{9x^3-6x^2-20x+1}{3x+2}\,dx
&=\left[x^3-2x^2-4x+3\ln(3x+2)\right]_1^6\\
&=(120+3\ln20)-(-5+3\ln5)\\
&=125+3\ln4\\
&=\boxed{125+\ln64}.
\end{aligned}
$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p2-int-q01"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-21.pdf`, Q7(a–b), and matching mark scheme.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p2-int-q02}
### Question 2 · 9709/22/M/J/20 Q8(a–c)

(a) Show that

$$
3\sin2\theta\cot\theta=6\cos^2\theta.
$$

**[2]**

(b) Solve the equation

$$
3\sin2\theta\cot\theta=5
$$

for $0<\theta<\pi$. **[3]**

(c) Find the exact value of

$$
\int_{\frac14\pi}^{\frac12\pi}3\sin x\cot\frac12x\,dx.
$$

**[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

Using $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$,

$$
3\sin2\theta\cot\theta
=3(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
=\boxed{6\cos^2\theta}.
$$

(b) By part (a),

$$
6\cos^2\theta=5
\Longrightarrow\cos^2\theta=\frac56.
$$

For $0<\theta<\pi$, this gives

$$
\boxed{\theta=\cos^{-1}\sqrt{\frac56}\quad\text{or}\quad
\theta=\pi-\cos^{-1}\sqrt{\frac56}}.
$$

(c)

Use $\sin x=2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)$:

$$
\sin x\cot\frac x2
=2\sin\frac x2\cos\frac x2\cdot\frac{\cos(x/2)}{\sin(x/2)}
=2\cos^2\frac x2
=1+\cos x.
$$

Therefore the integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}3(1+\cos x)\,dx
&=\left[3x+3\sin x\right]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\\
&=3\left(\frac\pi2+1-\frac\pi4-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right).
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{\frac34\pi+3-\frac32\sqrt2}.
$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p2-int-q02"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-22.pdf`, Q8(a–c), and matching mark scheme.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p2-int-q03}
### Question 3 · 9709/22/M/J/22 Q4(a–b)

(a) Use the trapezium rule with three intervals to show that the value of

$$
\int_1^4\ln x\,dx
$$

is approximately $\ln12$.

(b) Use a graph of $y=\ln x$ to show that $\ln12$ is an under-estimate of the true value of the integral. **[4+2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) With three intervals on $[1,4]$, $h=1$ and the values are

$$
y_0=\ln1,quad y_1=\ln2,quad y_2=\ln3,quad y_3=\ln4.
$$

The trapezium rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_3
&=\frac12\left[\ln1+2\ln2+2\ln3+\ln4\right]\\
&=\frac12\left[0+2\ln2+2\ln3+2\ln2\right]\\
&=\ln2+\ln3+\ln2\\
&=\boxed{\ln12}.
\end{aligned}
$$

(b) The graph $y=\ln x$ is concave down on $x>0$. Therefore each straight chord used by the trapezium rule lies below the curve, so the trapezium areas are smaller than the true area. Hence $\ln12$ is

$$
\boxed{\text{an under-estimate}}.
$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p2-int-q03"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_22.pdf`, Q4(a–b), and matching mark scheme.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p2-int-q04}
### Question 4 · 9709/22/M/J/24 Q5(a–b)

The polynomial $p(x)$ is defined by

$$
p(x)=9x^3+18x^2+5x+4.
$$

(a) Find the quotient when $p(x)$ is divided by $(3x+2)$, and show that the remainder is $6$. **[3]**

(b) Find the value of

$$
\int_0^2\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}\,dx,
$$

giving your answer in the form $a+\ln b$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) Polynomial division gives

$$
p(x)=(3x+2)(3x^2+4x-1)+6.
$$

Thus the quotient is $3x^2+4x-1$ and the remainder is $6$.

(b)

From polynomial division,

$$
p(x)=(3x+2)(3x^2+4x-1)+6.
$$

Thus

$$
\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}=3x^2+4x-1+\frac6{3x+2}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^2\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}\,dx
&=\left[x^3+2x^2-x+2\ln(3x+2)\right]_0^2\\
&=(8+8-2+2\ln8)-2\ln2\\
&=14+2\ln4\\
&=\boxed{14+\ln16}.
\end{aligned}
$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p2-int-q04"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p22.pdf`, Q5(a–b), and matching mark scheme.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p2-int-q05}
### Question 5 · 9709/21/M/J/24 Q7(a–b)

The polynomial $p(x)$ is defined by

$$
p(x)=9x^3+6x^2+12x+k,
$$

where $k$ is a constant.

(a) Find the quotient when $p(x)$ is divided by $(3x+2)$ and show that the remainder is $(k-8)$.

(b) It is given that

$$
\int_1^6\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}\,dx=a+\ln64,
$$

where $a$ is an integer. Find the values of $a$ and $k$. **[3+6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) Polynomial division gives

$$
9x^3+6x^2+12x+k=(3x+2)(3x^2+4)+(k-8).
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{\text{quotient}=3x^2+4,\qquad \text{remainder}=k-8}.
$$

(b) Using the result from (a),

$$
\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}=3x^2+4+\frac{k-8}{3x+2}.
$$

Integrate and apply the limits:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_1^6\frac{p(x)}{3x+2}\,dx
&=\left[x^3+4x+\frac{k-8}{3}\ln(3x+2)\right]_1^6\\
&=235+\frac{k-8}{3}\ln4.
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\ln64=3\ln4$, comparison gives

$$
\frac{k-8}{3}=3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{k=17}.
$$

The integer part is therefore

$$
\boxed{a=235}.
$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p2-int-q05"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p21.pdf`, Q7(a–b), and matching mark scheme.</div>
